messages.subject: ledgerly sandbox recon - it's not clean
messages.body:
ran the reconciliation job against the ledgerly sandbox again last night. it's not clean.

- refunds: 6 of 41 test refunds failed to reconcile. ledgerly's batch settlement nets refunds against the next day's charges, so amounts don't match line by line. our recon expects gross line items.
- multi-currency: the PLN and SEK test invoices round trip with a cent-level rounding difference on fx conversion. sounds trivial but it fails the recon every time.
- 3 settlement reports this week didn't match the ledger at all, off by varying amounts. maya chen's team says it's a sandbox export bug and prod is fine, which is exactly what you'd say.

i can hack the recon to tolerate netting and rounding but then it stops catching real errors. fwiw.

messages.subject: RE: ledgerly sandbox recon - it's not clean
messages.body:
Thanks Jonas. Analysis:

- The refund netting is a schema mismatch, not a bug on their side. Fixable, but it means rewriting the reconciliation job before we can trust any settlement report. That is roughly a week of work I do not want to rush.
- The FX rounding needs a decision on where rounding happens (their side or ours) and a rule documented with Ledgerly.
- The 3 mismatched reports worry me most. If we cut over on 1 May as planned and even one real settlement is wrong, we are reconciling a live provider with a tool we know was failing the week before.

My take: the 1 May cutover is dead. We fix the recon, rerun it clean for at least one full sandbox cycle, and then go. I know that lands after the May billing run.

Cheers, Dev

messages.subject: RE: ledgerly sandbox recon - it's not clean
messages.body:
Dear Dev,

I understand the reasoning and I will not argue with the technical assessment, but I must flag the cash-flow implication: every additional month on PayForge costs us approximately €1,860 in fees versus Ledgerly, and we would now be running dual testing into June. That is real money for a company our size, and it is also a visible line item against the savings I promised the board for this year.

I would gently suggest that if we do delay, we set the new date firmly and resist moving it twice - a sliding cutover is worse for the books than a late one. Could you indicate what the earliest credible date would be?

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: ledgerly sandbox recon - it's not clean
messages.body:
Hi Dev,

Confirming what my colleague said on the ticket: the three mismatched exports were caused by a known sandbox reporting bug, fix is in their release train this week. Production settlement reporting is unaffected - we can show you prod-mode reporting under NDA if that helps your review.

On refunds: we can also emit a gross refund line item alongside the netted settlement if that simplifies your reconciliation. Worth a call?

Best,
Maya Chen
Account Manager, Ledgerly

messages.subject: RE: ledgerly sandbox recon - it's not clean
messages.body:
Good news from Maya - they can emit gross refund lines and the sandbox export bug has a fix shipping. That removes two of the three blockers. The recon rewrite still needs to happen and be proven over a clean cycle.

So: cutover moves to after the June billing cycle. I will own the recon rewrite and give Helen a firm date as soon as the first clean sandbox run completes. Helen - I hear you on the sliding date, you will get one date from me and I will hold to it.

Cheers, Dev

messages.body:
